heroText: Juba is South Sudan's capital, spread along the White Nile's west bank at the country's southern crossroads. First-time visitors should pay respects at the John Garang Mausoleum, cross the Nile at Juba Bridge for river views, and browse produce and crafts at Konyo Konyo Market. Juba International Airport sits close to the city centre, and travel here calls for careful planning given the country's ongoing security and infrastructure challenges.

areas.name: Juba Town
areas.text: Juba Town is the compact central district holding government offices, banks and the main market, the natural base for a short stay.

areas.name: Tongping
areas.text: Tongping sits near the airport and river, home to UN offices, NGOs and many of the city's international hotels.
areas.bestFor: official visits, NGO stays, airport access

areas.name: Munuki
areas.text: Munuki is a busy residential suburb west of the centre, useful for longer stays needing more local, lower-cost accommodation.

areas.name: Hai Malakal
areas.text: Hai Malakal is a central neighborhood close to the Nile riverside, convenient for river views and short walks to downtown offices.

airports.name: Juba International Airport (JUB)
airports.search: Juba International Airport, Juba, South Sudan
airports.text: Juba International Airport sits at the edge of the city centre, with hotel transfers and vetted taxis arranged in advance for most visitors.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Juba International Airport (JUB) and central Juba before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Most visits to Juba centre on Tongping or Juba Town, where international hotels, NGO offices and government buildings cluster close to the airport and river. Munuki and Hai Malakal suit longer, lower-key stays for those with local contacts and confirmed transport.
hotelIntro: Juba hotel choice is shaped by logistics and security: Tongping suits NGO and official visitors wanting airport proximity, Juba Town suits business trips needing central offices and banks, and Munuki or Hai Malakal suit longer, more local stays arranged through trusted contacts.
rentalCars: Independent car rental is uncommon; most visitors arrange a vetted driver through their hotel, employer or a local fixer for any movement around the city.

travelTips.title: Security planning
travelTips.text: Arrange travel and accommodation in advance through a trusted employer, NGO or hotel, and check current advisories before booking.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Base in Tongping or Juba Town, where most international hotels and organisations operate with established transport arrangements.

travelTips.title: River views
travelTips.text: Take a short boat trip or riverside walk near Juba Bridge for views over the White Nile at sunset.

travelTips.title: Cash and connectivity
travelTips.text: Carry US dollars for most payments, since South Sudanese pounds are used mainly for small local purchases.

nearbyIdeas.text: A short boat trip on the White Nile offers a different perspective on Juba, with river life and birdlife visible from the water.

history.text: Explorers and campaigners Samuel Baker and Florence Baker used the nearby island of Gondokoro as a base during their expeditions to what is now South Sudan and northern Uganda from 1863 to 1865 and.
From the establishment of Anglo-Egyptian Sudan in 1899, the British administered southern Sudan separately from the north.

history.label: 1920s
history.text: In the late 1920s, Anglo-Egyptian officials ordered Bari residents to relocate so that a new town could be constructed to serve as the capital of Mongalla Province.
Major construction of the new city of Juba was underway by 1927.
Traders from Rejaf relocated to the new city in 1929, and the Governor's office of Mongalla was moved there in 1930.
In 1946, without consulting Southern opinion, the British administration began instead to implement a policy of uniting the north and the south.
In 1955, a mutiny of southern soldiers in Torit sparked the First Sudanese Civil War, which did not end until 1972.
Until 1956, Juba was in Anglo-Egyptian Sudan, which was jointly administered by the United Kingdom and the Kingdom of Egypt.

In 2005, Juba became the interim seat and the capital of the Autonomous Government of Southern Sudan after the signing of the Comprehensive Peace Agreement (before the agreement, Rumbek had been the proposed interim.
Juba became South Sudan's national capital on 9 July 2011, when South Sudan formally declared its independence from the Republic of the Sudan.
In November 2017, the former chief of general staff Paul Malong Awan was removed from the city, and since then has become a fortified stronghold for President Kiir.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Public buildings, such as the Ivory Bank, Notos Lounge, the old Sudan Airways Building, Paradise Hotel, and the Nile Commercial Bank and Buffalo Commercial Bank, were all built by Greeks.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Under the leadership of the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, the United Nations established a camp known as "OCHA Camp", which served as a base for many United Nations agencies.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: However, influential parties including the South Sudanese government expressed dissatisfaction with the city's suitability as a national capital, and the government proposed that a new planned city be built as a replacement capital elsewhere.
